projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: The persistent count of 25–27 connected devices paired with zero camera activity over four hours strongly indicates false presence detection, likely from network ghosting, external device cross-talk, or misconfigured guest/IoT networks rather than actual occupancy. Steve should verify the connected device list to rule out unauthorized access or network misconfiguration.

The combination of 20–27 persistent devices, zero camera motion, and a four-person household strongly indicates a network-level false positive (likely MAC randomization or a guest network) rather than actual physical presence, which could trigger unnecessary automations or mask real security events.

The sustained high device count (20–27) paired with zero camera activity on a Thursday evening strongly suggests the connected devices are parked outside (e.g., in vehicles or a garage) or the network is picking up strong neighbor signals, rather than the household being actively present indoors.

The sustained count of 25–27 connected devices far exceeds the household's normal footprint, and combined with zero camera activity on a weekday afternoon, this strongly indicates either a large unregistered gathering or a network registration anomaly that Steve should verify to rule out unauthorized access.

The sustained presence of 21–27 mobile devices combined with zero camera activity on a Thursday afternoon strongly indicates a large indoor gathering or network overcounting; Steve should verify if this is a planned visit or a false positive to rule out connectivity anomalies or unmonitored activity.

The sustained high device count (19-23) combined with zero camera activity suggests the devices are likely stationary or represent network artifacts rather than an active gathering, indicating no immediate need for concern.

The sustained presence of 19-23 mobile devices on a Thursday afternoon strongly suggests an unexplained gathering or guests, as this far exceeds the expected count for a four-person household. This warrants a quick check to confirm it's a planned visit and not a network anomaly.

The consistent presence of ~21 devices during typical school hours on a Thursday, combined with zero camera activity, indicates the household is at home today (likely remote work/school or a break) with no unusual activity or security concerns.

The connected device count dropped from ~27 to ~21 between 07:46 and 08:13, indicating a coordinated departure of multiple household members, likely the children heading to school and/or adults leaving for work. This aligns with typical Thursday morning routines and confirms normal household activity rather than a network glitch.

The persistent 25-27 device count at 4 AM combined with zero camera or activity signals indicates the presence detector is likely counting stationary IoT devices as mobile phones, which will skew occupancy-based automations.
